strongest_angle: Investigating how Irish immigrant labor led by Father Bernard Donnelly carved through 120-foot limestone bluffs along the Missouri River to build Kansas City's streets.

key_facts.fact: Limestone bluffs up to 120 feet tall once hugged the Missouri River by Kansas City, creating a major barrier to urban expansion in the mid-1800s.
In the mid-1800s, a Catholic priest named Father Bernard Donnelly recruited hundreds of Irish immigrants to dig streets through the rocky bluffs.
When Kansas City Mayor Milton Payne took office in 1855, he authorized almost an entire year's budget to cut back the edge of the bluff and pave a quarter mile of the levee.
